# Quarto + AI

Introduce the idea that AI agents can now help create documents, websites, and dashboards.

Show the AI-generated handwriting-sheet example and introduce the basic artifact-generation problem.

# Quarto disentangles content and format

Show the source/render architecture and explain that Quarto moves the boundary to a controllable source.

---

# Ask for the source, not the artifact

State the key principle: ask the agent for the `.qmd`, then let Quarto render the artifact.

---

# This is not a 3,000-line dashboard

Show the vehicletrends site as a collection of small `.qmd` pages rather than one giant dashboard.

---

# Every page gets a URL

Show individual vehicletrends page URLs and emphasize that the dashboard behaves like a website.

---

# No UI. No server.

Contrast a traditional application architecture with a Quarto document containing client-side widgets.

---

# Small pieces have small context windows

Show that an agent can work on one 200–600-line page instead of loading the entire dashboard into context.

---

# Interactivity lives in the browser

Show an interactive ECharts/echarts4r/Plotly-style widget and emphasize that the browser handles the interaction.

---

# Document layout comes for free

Briefly show tabs, TOC, columns, sidebar/navigation, and other Quarto document primitives used to organize the dashboard.

---

# Have a heavier artifact? Put it in a box.

Show the complex census-tract map living in its own project and being embedded into the dashboard.

---

# It's just static files

Show the browser/client-side architecture and explain that the finished site can be hosted as static files on GitHub Pages or Netlify.

---

# Quarto composes things that don't need to understand each other

Synthesize the dashboard architecture and connect it explicitly to AI: decomposition keeps individual pieces understandable and manageable.

---

# Control → Cost → Correctness

Reintroduce the three-part spine and transition from the architectural idea to quantitative and technical evidence.

---

# Token experiment

Show the comparison between repeatedly generating finished artifacts and generating one `.qmd` source.

---

# One source, many outputs

Show how one source can deterministically produce multiple rendered artifacts.

---

# Bad Africa map

Show the plausible-but-wrong map and introduce the problem of artifacts that have no failure mode.

---

# Same map from source

Show the source alongside the correctly rendered map.

---

# Quarto is checkable twice

Show machine checking through `quarto render` and human checking through a plain-text diff.

---

# Back to the dashboard

Return to the vehicletrends dashboard from the beginning and invite the audience to see it differently.

---

# Peel apart the dashboard

Reveal that the dashboard is composed of small `.qmd` pages, separate data, widgets, navigation, and independently built heavy artifacts.

---

# The dashboard architecture

Show a diagram connecting the agent, small `.qmd` sources, Quarto, data, widgets/external artifacts, and the browser.

---

# Agents should write the source, not the artifact

State the final principle and connect it to control, context, cost, and correctness.

---

# The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Quarto

Close on the broader thesis: Quarto is unusually effective for AI because it gives probabilistic agents a clean source to write and a deterministic system to render and check.
